newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat's Romiti calls for help for Italy's south.
newsitem.headline: Fiat's Romiti calls for help for Italy's south.

text.p: Cesare Romiti, the chairman of Italy's biggest private industrial group Fiat, has called for more flexible labour laws to help revive Italy's poor south.

Romiti wants labour laws dating back to July 1993, which stipulate similar wage levels throughout Italy, to be revised to give more flexibility to Italy's labour force and aid job creation in Italy's impoverished southern half.

"The accord of July 1993 on the cost of labour is due for revision," Romiti was reported as saying in the Corriere della Sera daily newspaper on Sunday at a weekend conference on Italy's south in the southern city of Naples.
He added that labour flexibility was essential to create new jobs in Italy's southern region.
"The south is not a problem, it is an opportunity. There, is the future of Italy," he added.
But Sergio Cofferati, head of one of Italy's main three union confederations, the CGIL, said that Fiat wanted Italy's workers to pay the price of greater European integration.
Cofferati has cautioned before on calls for a more flexible labour market, warning that wage flexibility should not try to substitute for national working contracts.

Fiat has been a big investor in the south of Italy and produces over half its national output of cars there, with major car plants in Melfi, Cassino and Pomigliano D'Arco near Naples and a smaller plant in Termini Imerese on Sicily.
